agent-note:v1 — Agent: repo-design-architect-code (pass 66); state: routing — the Python wrong-shape wave filed 2026-11-06/07 belongs to this audit's inventory; no new design originated.

Pass 66 audited the window #6812–#6861 (origin/main 65beb42c1) and found 18 filings of the #3068 parsed-shape mechanism in the repo's Python tools — the largest single-mechanism wave since #3068 itself. They are NOT a new design: #3068's stated rule already covers them, including its Python corollary (`isinstance(v, dict)`), its field-depth clause ("the validated shape is exactly the shape dereferenced: … the type of each field that is read, bound, or stored"), its named-error corollary (the tool's own error vocabulary — `ColdStoreError`, `fail()`, `SafetyError` — never a raw `TypeError`/`AttributeError`/`KeyError`), and its probe matrix. This audit's own scope names exactly these surfaces ("every parse-then-deref boundary in bin/, scripts/, pkgs/ tools … `json.loads`"). Originating a parallel Python design would duplicate #3068/#3069.

For this audit's inventory, the wave's instances (all `task/small-fix` with complete per-site acceptances; each keeps its own queue lifecycle — this note does not reassign any of them):

- github-backup (ghb_common gates exist; the legs are field-depth residuals of #6637/#6716/#6652 and bare-load bypasses of the shared validators): #6821 (`last_fetch` field), #6831 (reconcile previous-plan read), #6834 (`reference`/`branch` fields), #6835 (drain_queue bare `json.load`), #6849 (app_setup config/bws/conversion); #6814 (generate field-level) closed in-window. Cross-reference: this subset is also inside design #3282's estate — its closing audit #3283 dispositions the state-access overlap, this audit dispositions the shape rule; decide once, in whichever lands first.
- cold-store-reaper: #6845 (load_state/load_credentials + `folders`), #6846 (token-endpoint responses), #6855 (Drive API responses). (#2618, this tool's D1 slice, was #3068 Phase 2.)
- mcpx guard/CI scripts (stored-record ratchets — a wrong shape must never silently re-baseline): #6822 (e2e-shard-packer seed), #6850 (conformance-record), #6851 (gotest-report), #6852 (spec-parity).
- research_workflow tools: #6854, #6856, #6857. (#2800, this tool family's manifest/profile slice, was #3068 Phase 2.)
- cargo-target-janitor: #6844 (raw shape errors, not `SafetyError`). update-nixpkgs-inputs: #6847 (flake.lock nodes; mid-run partial update).

Two Python-specific traps recur in the wave and belong in this audit's probe matrix when it lands: `bool` is an `int` subclass (a bool `last_fetch` silently reads as epoch 1 — #6821; count fields must exclude bool, as #6850's acceptance pins), a `str` is iterable (a string name-set silently becomes its characters — #6850/#6852; an empty list stored record silently reads as "no record" and resets a ratchet — #6851), and `json.load` accepts `Infinity`/`NaN` by default (#6822).

Disposition requested from this audit: inventory these 17 open filings as covered-by-#3068 instances (fixed per site under their own acceptances), and state the field-depth + no-bare-load-bypass reading once in the contract statement — the github-backup chain (#6637 entry-level → #6716/#6814 field-level → #6821/#6834 field-level again, plus #6831/#6835 bypasses) is the evidence that per-site patching at entry depth does not converge for Python either.

These are covered-by-#3068 instances for this audit's inventory, on the same terms as pass 66's note (comment on this issue, 2026-11-07): each keeps its own queue lifecycle and complete per-site acceptance; this note does not reassign any of them.

New instances this window:

- #6862 research_workflow scaffold `--outline` JSON — the same tool whose profile/state/trigger (#6854) and note/resolution (#6857) shapes were hardened in the pass-66 wave; the outline input was the uncovered sibling in the same file.

- #6868 opencode-claimant poll.py session `time` — one wrong-shaped entry crashes the whole poll (no per-entry guard). Cross-reference: this is also claimant estate — see the note on #4916 (design #4912's closing audit) recording #6865/#6868 for its server-call inventory.
